sourcesActuallyRead.title: Warum können Rinder von Gras leben?
sourcesActuallyRead.readScope: Original HTML core article read, particularly web lines147,150–154,162–168. Lists the three forestomachs and abomasum; explains microbial fermentation of structural plant material and distinguishes later enzymatic processing. The source's everyday plural stomach language is not copied as a new anatomical count claim.
sourcesActuallyRead.excluded: No cow volumes, calf ages, feeding/ration instructions or direct numerical extrapolation to roe deer.

sourcesActuallyRead.title: Das Reh – Durch Anpassung zum Erfolg, Tipps und Anregungen für Lehrpersonen
sourcesActuallyRead.readScope: Physical PDF page10 = printed8, the complete digestive paragraph from Nahrung, read as original extracted text and visually in a local Poppler PNG. Names rumen, reticulum, omasum and abomasum for roe deer; separates microbial rumen processing and later digestive juices. The related museums are one source family, never counted independently from each other.
sourcesActuallyRead.excluded: No old survey figures, intake amounts, season guarantees, hunting rules, handling advice, or strict twice-only/linear passage claim is introduced.

sourcesActuallyRead.title: Die Pansenwand im Fokus,12January2023
sourcesActuallyRead.readScope: Original university research communication read, particularly core paragraphs42–44 and the surrounding microbial-population findings. It identifies microorganisms as principal actors in rumen processing. This is the institution's explanation of its own work, not a claimed experimental replication of BZL or a substitute for reading an inaccessible underlying paper.
sourcesActuallyRead.excluded: No quantitative energy fractions, microbial composition predictions, acetate results, interventions or feeding recommendations.

sourcesActuallyRead.title: Anatomie des Digestitionsapparates
sourcesActuallyRead.readScope: Original short HTML page read, especially lines6–7. It calls the pig stomach single-cavity and composite, then describes the different mucosal areas. The distinction is chamber number versus wall types; composite is not a claim of multiple stomach cavities.
sourcesActuallyRead.excluded: No pig ages, stomach capacities, colour-based identification guarantees, feeding behaviour or clinical claims.

sourcesActuallyRead.title: Ernährung und Fütterung der Schweine, section6.1.1 Aufbau, Entwicklung und Funktion des Verdauungstraktes
sourcesActuallyRead.organisation: Thünen repository, Brade/Flachowsky edited swine reference work

sourcesActuallyRead.excluded: No dimensions, volume fractions, ages, developmental curves, feed formulas, recommendations or quantitative absorption shares are reused.

questions.questionDirection: positive: choose the correct stomach-compartment group
questions.whyPlausible: Three names belong to the taught stomach system, but the intestinal segment replaces the omasum; this is more anatomically adjacent than the existing liver/lung/kidney distractor and does not duplicate it.
questions.whyUnambiguous: Both independent sources list the omasum with rumen, reticulum and abomasum. Replacing it with the small intestine does not give the requested group.
questions.claimLimit: Only the taught ruminant stomach model; no new organ counts, measurements, position/scale claims or assertion that a photograph proves function.

questions.questionDirection: positive: choose what makes fibre-rich plant material useful in the rumen
questions.fourthChoice: Allein durch körpereigenen Magensaft, ohne mikrobielle Gärung
questions.whyPlausible: Distinguishes host digestive secretions from microbial processing, rather than repeating the existing colour or once-only-transit distractors.
questions.whyUnambiguous: BZL and Vetmeduni independently describe microbes as key rumen processors. Host gastric juice alone without that process does not describe the taught rumen mechanism.
questions.claimLimit: No blanket denial of host enzymes elsewhere, no exclusive claim about all plant substrates and no feeding, treatment or chemical measurements.

questions.questionDirection: positive: choose the correct wild-boar digestive ground-plan description
questions.fourthChoice: Ein mehrhöhliger Magen, weil seine Schleimhaut zusammengesetzt ist
questions.whyPlausible: Tests the actual specialist terminology confusion: different mucosal regions do not imply multiple cavities. It differs from inventing a rumen or omitting the intestine.
questions.whyUnambiguous: UZH explicitly calls the pig stomach single-cavity/composite and describes its mucosal zones. Independent Thünen text and Fig6.2 show a single-cavity stomach with distinct wall regions. The existing teaching already confines domestic-pig references to ground-plan comparison.
questions.claimLimit: No extrapolation of livestock dimensions, intake or individual wild-boar findings; no new numerical claim.

questions.questionDirection: NEGATIVE: choose the statement that is too sweeping; the existing correct option is the false universal claim about absence of microbial digestion
questions.fourthChoice: Im Dünndarm des Schweins werden Nährstoffe aufgenommen
questions.whyPlausible: Adds a true physiological function rather than merely repeating the existing anatomical statement that pigs have small and large intestine. The learner must still identify the unchanged false universal claim.
questions.whyUnambiguous: Thünen explicitly locates nutrient absorption in the small intestine. The independently authored Minnesota monogastric chapter identifies it as a digestion/absorption site and includes pigs in the model. The new wording has no only/all or quantitative guarantee.
questions.claimLimit: It is a correct alternative deliberately NOT selected for this negative question. No all-nutrients/only-site/efficiency/amount claim, no feeding recommendation.
